Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the data patterns:

## Example 1 (2025-06-06)
History shows price volatility around 70-76 range
Sentiment goes from 0.67 → 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.33 → 1.00 → 0.33 → 0.67 → 1.00 → 0.33 → 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67 → 0.67 → 0.67 → 1.00 → 0.67 → 0.67 → 0.33

Model forecasts are generally higher than true outcomes. Let me look at specific patterns:

At the start (days 1-5):
- Model: [73.26, 73.97, 72.57, 74.22, 75.55]
- True: [73.50, 74.23, 72.66, 74.36, 75.39]

The model underestimates when prices are rising rapidly. The model seems to lag behind the true price movements, especially on upward kicks.

Looking at sentiment correlations:
- When sentiment is 1.00 (high bullish), model still underforecasts the true peak
- The model appears to dampen movements too much

Let me look at Example 2 for confirmation:
2025-06-05
Model: [72.64, 73.37, 74.25, 72.98, 74.74, 76.16, 76.82, 76.38, 75.76, 75.71]
True: [72.74, 73.50, 74.23, 72.66, 74.36, 75.39, 75.94, 75.34, 74.64, 74.61]

Still seeing the model forecast being lower than true outcomes, especially on the upward sides.
 
I notice a consistent pattern of model forecasts being 0.2-0.6 points below true prices. When prices dip, the model captures this better, but struggles with price increases. The divergence seems most pronounced when sentiment shifts from low to high, suggesting the model may have difficulty fully accounting for rapid price momentum.
